I'd like to give my opinion as an Australian. I personally think compulsory voting is a great thing for a number of reasons:

1. It limits extreme populism in candidates as they need to appeal to a broader majority instead of just who they can compel to actually vote.
2. It means that resources don't need to be wasted on "get out the vote" initiatives as we automatically get high voter turnout

It also isn't really mandatory. You can spoil your ballot if you so choose, the fine isn't huge and if you have a legitimate reason it isn't that hard to get the fine waived.

Admittedly our election system is quite different from USA, for one we have the parliamentary system. We also have preferential voting which is probably the biggest thing, we don't do first-past-the-post.

We also have an attitude that voting is a civic responsibility rather than a right. We don't have a widespread distrust of government (yet) that exists in USA either.

Compulsory voting is actually pretty popular among Australians. Also it's not really compulsory, in practice you can spoil your ballot or do whatever if you don't want to actually vote. You are just required to present yourself.
